newsitem.title: UK: ZINC TURNS LOWER ON LME, OTHERS FOLLOW SUIT.
newsitem.headline: ZINC TURNS LOWER ON LME, OTHERS FOLLOW SUIT.

text.p: Base metal prices were mostly lower during Tuesday LME pre-market trading, with a tumble in zinc indicative of the general trend, traders said.
Latest inventory data was also negative in most cases with copper, zinc, nickel, and aluminium stocks all rising.

Zinc stocks rose by 1,400 tonnes, underlining talk that there may be further deliveries of metal into the Singapore warehouse which would reflect Chinese shipments against upcoming LME short positions.
Three months prices fell to a low of $1,514 a tonne at one stage, and may even have dipped to $1,510, before settling at $1,520, a $24 loss from Monday's kerb.
In the short term the market's tendency to technically correct lower will be offset to some extent by the backwardation. Cash/threes was at a still-steep $145/150 premium on Tuesday.
Copper fell to $2,259 at one point, briefly threatening to trigger a more substantial sell-off, before prices regained $2,270, a $4 loss.
To some extent the market was helped by renewed problems at the OK Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea, where concentrate cannot be shipped because of dry weather.
However, a hefty 3,900-tonne warehouse stock increase, the latest in a long-running trend, suggests that the market will come under further pressure.
Aluminium dropped back to $1,725, unable to maintain the upward momentum of Monday afternoon as there was little sign of follow-through fund buying.
Also, there was a surprising 725-tonne rise in LME stocks, only the second increase in a persistent downtrend. Recent business was at $1,725, down $25 from yesterday's kerb.
Nickel stocks rose by 336 tonnes, and prices reacted lower, with business at $6,810, down $50. Tin also lost ground under some liquidation, and fell to $5,455 before settling at $5,475, a $35 loss.
Lead was an exception, holding just $1 down at $605. Alloy was indicated at a softer $1,525/35 a tonne.
